gates.row_count: Born-digital pdf-lib rendering: the schedule pages carry NO printed row rules (rowbands.py has no grid to score), so rows were counted by ink lines and independently cross-checked against the PDF's own embedded text layer (pdftotext -layout), which returns exactly 4 text lines on p2 and exactly 14 on p3 between the column header row and the footer block -- matching the 4 and 14 rows emitted, with no line dropped or duplicated. Also confirmed via pdftotext -bbox-layout that the 4 (resp. 14) line boxes are on a uniform 1.89%-of-page pitch with no gap.

escalation_note: Every schedule figure re-read at 600 dpi as tight cell crops (6 crops incl. 2 empty controls) and independently corroborated against the PDF's embedded text layer; every value read identically. No glyph was in doubt (born-digital type, not handwriting).
notes: OFFICE CONFIRMED AT THE PAGE: index.csv says 'County Attorney'; the cover's Office line reads verbatim 'Cache County Attorney' -- agrees, in scope. DATE AGREES with the chunk file (2026-03-04 vs the form's 03-04-2026 on the cover, the three footers, and the 'Signed at: 2026-03-04 00:09:51' stamp). REPORT TYPE: none of the three printed radios is marked; the filer instead typed the free-text line '3 Days Prior to Party Nominating Convention' into the right-hand block, so the report type is stated only in prose. FILING SHAPE: on BOTH schedules the filer ignored the ruled columns entirely and typed each transaction as ONE dash-delimited free-text line ('date-name-address-amount'), so column assignment is by the filer's own delimiters, not by cell position. FIELD-SHIFT SCREEN passed: p2 has 4 lines each carrying exactly one parseable date, one name, one address and one amount (4 names = 4 amounts); p3 has 14 lines each with exactly one date and one trailing amount; no date-shaped content appears in a name slot or vice versa. On p3 the vendor/purpose boundary is genuinely AMBIGUOUS on several lines because the filer used '-' both as the field delimiter and inside prose; the full verbatim line is preserved in each row's note so the split can be re-derived. Donor street addresses printed in the clear were discarded at read time (city/state only); the candidate's own home address, phone and email on the cover were likewise discarded.
